qa_pairs.question: What conditions must a student satisfy to register for a course when they have a possible prerequisite issue?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student may register only when there is no active academic, conduct, advising, or financial hold. A prerequisite is satisfied by a completed course with the catalogue's minimum grade, an approved transfer equivalent, or a recorded prerequisite waiver; instructor permission alone is not enough unless the programme director also records the waiver.

contexts.text: A student may register only when there is no active academic, conduct, advising, or financial hold.

A prerequisite is satisfied by a completed course with the minimum grade stated in the catalogue, an approved transfer equivalent, or a recorded prerequisite waiver. Instructor permission alone does not replace a prerequisite unless the programme director also records the waiver.

qa_pairs.question: What approvals and payment are required for a late add during the late-add window?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.

contexts.text: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.

The late-add fee is USD 40 per course and must be paid within two business days after the approvals described in `02_course_registration.md`. The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

qa_pairs.question: How does the timing of a course drop affect tuition reversal?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A course dropped by the end of standard add/drop receives a 100% tuition reversal. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

contexts.text: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

For Fall 2026, priority registration opens on July 20, regular registration closes on August 14, classes begin on August 17, and the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28. The census date is September 4.

qa_pairs.question: What should a student do if they believe a final grade contains a calculation error?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student should first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days and identify a permitted ground such as calculation error; disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

contexts.text: A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor. Alleged calculation error, procedural unfairness, discrimination, or inconsistency with the published syllabus may proceed to the formal grade-appeal route in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

qa_pairs.question: What must a student do to request a standard leave and later return from it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: For a standard leave, the student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide required documentation, and obtain programme approval. To return, the student must submit a return notice at least 20 calendar days before regular registration closes.

contexts.text: A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms. The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval.
To return from approved leave, a student submits a return notice at least 20 calendar days before regular registration closes.

qa_pairs.question: How can a financial hold affect graduation even when the student has completed the academic requirements?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official degree conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved. An unpaid balance after the grace period also creates a financial hold and blocks graduation clearance.

contexts.text: A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`.
An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance.

qa_pairs.question: A student discussed a late add in July but submits the request on August 2, 2026. Which registration policy and fee apply?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Registration Policy version 2.0 applies because the late-add request was made on or after August 1, 2026. The late add is allowed through the census date and charges USD 40 per course; the earlier July discussion does not determine the policy version.

contexts.text: Registration Policy version 1.0, effective before August 1, 2026, allowed late adds for seven calendar days after standard add/drop and charged USD 25. Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.
Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date.

qa_pairs.question: How do medical leave and voluntary leave differ for a Merit Scholarship?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. Voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date. A retroactive medical-leave request normally must be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation.

contexts.text: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date.

Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation.

qa_pairs.question: If a student withdraws from a course after the Fall 2026 census date but before October 30, what are the likely academic, tuition, and scholarship consequences?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Fall 2026's census date is September 4 and the last day to withdraw with a W is October 30. A withdrawal after census and through the deadline receives a W; it remains attempted credit and does not erase attempted credits from all progress calculations. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary withdrawal. The withdrawal may affect scholarship review because it counts as attempted but not completed credit and may cause failure at the end-of-term review.

contexts.text: The census date is September 4. The last day to withdraw from a course with a `W` grade is October 30, and final examinations run from December 7 through December 12.

After census and through the withdrawal deadline in `01_academic_calendar.md`, the course receives a `W`. After that deadline, withdrawal requires an exceptional-circumstances petition. Stopping attendance is not a withdrawal.

A course withdrawal after census normally produces a `W` and does not erase the attempted credits from all progress calculations. Financial consequences are governed by `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`, while scholarship consequences are governed by `04_scholarships.md`.
After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.
A withdrawal after census still counts as attempted credit but not completed credit and may cause failure at the end-of-term review.

qa_pairs.question: A student has 120 applicable credits and a 2.10 cumulative GPA but still has a pending grade appeal and a financial hold. Can the university confer the degree immediately?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Not necessarily. The student may satisfy some academic thresholds, but graduation also requires all programme-required courses and the capstone requirement, and degree conferral requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. The financial hold blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript. A pending grade appeal may also delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.

contexts.text: An undergraduate student is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.

Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`. A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.

qa_pairs.question: A parent pays a student's tuition and wants the student's academic record, while the student also wants to challenge an academic decision. What privacy and process rules apply?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information; the university may discuss the record only with the student or a person with valid recorded authorization. A change to an academic decision must use the relevant appeal process, and cases should be submitted through the portal while sensitive evidence is kept out of public chat and general support tickets.

contexts.text: The university may discuss a student's record only with the student or a person who has a valid, recorded authorization. A parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information. Students may download their own enrolment and billing records from the portal. Requests to correct inaccurate personal data go to the Records Office; requests to change an academic decision must use the relevant appeal process.
Students should submit cases through the portal and keep the case number. Sensitive evidence must not be sent through public chat or included in a general support ticket.

qa_pairs.question: I missed a published deadline because my laptop failed, so the deadline is automatically extended, correct?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. An individual internet or device problem does not automatically extend a deadline. A calendar-date deadline ends at 17:00 Northstar local time. An extension may be announced only when the student portal is unavailable for more than two continuous hours during the final six hours before the deadline and the Registrar documents the extension.

contexts.text: The Northstar Student Services Assistant provides general information from the official documents in this corpus. It may explain academic deadlines, course registration, tuition, scholarships, attendance, grading, leave, graduation, appeals, student support, privacy, and account security. The corpus is the assistant's only authoritative source for this educational lab.

A deadline stated as a calendar date ends at 17:00 Northstar local time unless the policy explicitly gives another time. A submission received after the deadline is late even if a student started it earlier. When the student portal is unavailable for more than two continuous hours during the final six hours before a published deadline, the Registrar may announce a documented extension. Individual internet or device problems do not automatically extend a deadline.
